course_name_original: ELETTRONICA E MISURE PER LA BIOMEDICA
prerequisites: Knowledge of the fundamentals of electrical circuits and passive components.
An Electrotechnics exam is a prerequisite to take the final exam.

learning_outcomes.text: The course aims to provide students with knowledge of the fundamental concepts of analog and digital electronics. For this purpose, the main electronic devices and circuits are described, with application examples and laboratory sessions. Upon passing the exam, the student should be able to analyze and design electronic circuits and systems.
The course aims to provide the student with knowledge of the measurement principles, devices, and instrumentation used for measuring the main electrical parameters in a biomedical environment.
Have deep knowledge of the definitions and basic concepts in the field of measurements.
Have deep knowledge of the basic concepts of measurement theory.
Have knowledge and understanding of the operating principle of basic electronic instrumentation.
Demonstrate the ability to define and select the best strategies to solve problems, using the results of electrical measurements as a starting point.
Be able to set up a measurement, choosing methods, instruments, and data processing techniques, and be able to determine the uncertainty of the final result, also in relation to current regulations.
Understand and be able to explain the validity and reliability of the measurements performed.
Demonstrate the ability to communicate results clearly and coherently.
Upon passing the exam, the student should be able to analyze and design electronic circuits and systems.

At the end of the training activity, the student should be able to understand the fundamental concepts of measurement theory and the potential biomedical applications of basic electronic instrumentation.

syllabus_topics: Measurement of electrical resistance and impedance
Operating principles of digital electronic instruments
Main biomedical instruments (electrocardiograph, electromyograph, pulse oximeter)
Protection from electrical risks in biomedical instrumentation
Introduction to electronics: analog and digital quantities
Differential amplifier, operational amplifier (OA) and transconductance amplifier (OTA)
Configurations with OA: inverting, non-inverting, buffer
Circuits with non-linear open-loop OAs: comparators, astable
Bipolar and field-effect transistors: introduction, Gm
Non-linear transcharacteristic: biasing and small-signal equivalent circuits
Transistor circuits (CS, CD, CE and CC)
Introduction to digital electronics: binary representation, combinational circuits, logic gates, K-maps, sequential circuits
Laboratory exercises: review of RC and CR circuits, circuits with OA, diode circuits, MOSFET CS, dual-stage amplifiers, combinational and sequential circuits, A/D and D/A converters
assessment_rules: The assessment of the learning process is carried out through continuous interaction between the teacher and students during lessons and laboratory exercises. The achievement of the learning objectives verifies the student's ability to understand and apply knowledge in the field of electrical measurements through an oral exam, during which three topics of the course, proposed by the teacher, will be discussed. The criteria for evaluation will be: the level of knowledge of measurement theory and the main instruments and measurement techniques presented in the course, the ability to apply knowledge, communication skills and the scientific language used, the clarity and completeness of the explanations, critical thinking. The final exam includes a written question, two oral questions, and a discussion on laboratory reports.
